summary: A searchable list of every command in the product, opened with ⌘K / Ctrl+K from anywhere, that runs the chosen command and closes.
useWhen: the product has more actions and destinations than its navigation shows at once
people who use it daily want to reach anything without the pointer
mounted once, near the root, with every command the product has

useInstead.when: the user picks a value that stays chosen — an assignee, a country
useInstead.why: a combobox selects and keeps a value in a form; a palette runs a command once and goes away

useInstead.when: a few actions belong to one object — a row's Edit, Duplicate, Delete
useInstead.why: those actions belong beside the thing they act on, where people look for them

useInstead.when: the search is over records — agents, runs — shown as a page of results
useInstead.why: a filtered table is a page with its own URL, and a palette is gone the moment it is used

guarantees: a modal dialog named by `label`: focus is trapped, the page behind is hidden from assistive tech, Escape and a scrim click close it, and focus returns to what had it
focus stays in the search field, a combobox whose always-open listbox is driven by aria-activedescendant — typing and choosing never compete for focus
sections are role=group, named by their heading
disabled commands are listed with aria-disabled, skipped by the arrow keys, and do nothing on click
the number of matches is announced through a polite live region as the query changes
`onAction` runs after the palette has closed and handed focus back, so an action that moves focus keeps it
shortcut hints are read as key names — "Command Shift N" — not as symbols
requires: every command also reachable without the palette — it is a faster route, never the only one
a visible way to open it for people who do not know the shortcut, such as a header button showing the keys

antiPatterns.dont: showing a `shortcut` on a command without binding that shortcut yourself
antiPatterns.why: the palette displays a command's shortcut and does not listen for it; a hint for a key that does nothing is worse than no hint

antiPatterns.dont: moving focus from inside a command's handler by running it before closing, or wrapping onAction to close the palette first
antiPatterns.why: onAction already runs after close. While the dialog is mounted its focus scope pulls focus back to the search field

antiPatterns.dont: rendering <CommandPalette> only when a state flag is true
antiPatterns.do: mount it always and drive `isOpen`, or let it open itself on the shortcut
start with a verb — "Go to Agents", "Switch to dark theme"
antiPatterns.why: a row says what pressing Enter will do; a noun leaves the reader guessing whether it opens, toggles or deletes

antiPatterns.dont: two palettes on one page, or a second listener for ⌘K
antiPatterns.why: both toggle on the same key press and cancel each other out

emptyLabel.expects: what to show when nothing matches
